source_span: That means Wednesday starts with the 10-year above 5%, oil above $100, a Fed hike largely expected and duration positioning already heavily negative. The hike itself is no longer much of a surprise. The reaction could be.
source_chain: Yields already spiked above 5% and duration positioning sits at DB's 5th percentile (near-record bearish/short), therefore a hike is no longer the surprise and there is little incremental selling left to do, therefore the hawkish outcome itself could trigger a bond rally rather than a selloff ('hike to save the bond market'). Invalidation is level- and signal-based: the thesis breaks if yields sustain a push through 5.15-5.20% or the Fed explicitly endorses a longer/more aggressive hiking cycle or the energy shock intensifies; it's confirmed if yields fall back through 4.81%/4.73%.
pulse_chain: The Fed delivered the most hawkish outcome available (hike, 16-of-18 dot majority, higher long-run rate), therefore Treasuries rallied anyway because everyone who wanted to be short already was (DB 5th-percentile positioning), therefore the 10-year fell back to 4.95% from above 5%. The pulse's invalidation is a different event: the October FOMC meeting and its 51%-priced odds, framed as what will decide whether this week's rally is bears closing out or a real turn, with Goldman (October) vs. JPMorgan (December) as the debate.
why: The pulse reproduces the note's A-therefore-B step (extreme short positioning turns a hawkish hike into relief-rally fuel) faithfully but swaps the note's own invalidation — specific yield levels (4.81/4.73 vs. 5.15-5.20) or an explicit Fed signal/energy-shock — for an unrelated one, the October FOMC's 51% pricing, which the source note never names as what confirms or breaks its thesis.
